Consult Summary:
- Right knee radicular symptoms with clicking and pain during training; intermittent swelling previously; distal paresthesia (toes). Plan includes physio assessment, ice therapy, activity modification, and consideration of imaging and stronger anti-inflammatory.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Right knee pain with clicking after increased training for marathon; difficulty running long distances; occasional toe tingling.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms started about 2 weeks ago; pain during runs (~20 minutes in), worsens with longer runs; previously experienced transient swelling.
- Associated symptoms: Tingling in right toes after a run once; no persistent numbness; no locking reported by patient; able to walk and perform daily activities.
- Negative findings: No current knee swelling; no locking or instability claimed; ROM eventually described as full.
- Past medical history: Prior ice hockey injury with a large bruise several months ago; history of UTI with concern for kidney stones (ER visit); Lasik surgery; farsighted; otherwise stable.
- Medications: Ibuprofen (as needed; 400 mg noted), Aleve (naproxen) sometimes; Melatonin; Vitamin D; Xanax occasionally; Acetaminophen possibility mentioned by patient; Cannabis use (smoking joints).
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Social history: Marathon training; multiple sports; cannabis use.

Examination:
- Right knee: Symptoms described as middle of knee with occasional shift to the lateral side during movement; no locking reported; ability to bend and straighten described as intact (patient stated full ROM). Past transient swelling at onset of symptoms; current exam not detailing warmth or redness. No other joint findings noted. Distal neurovascular status not detailed beyond sensation reported (toes tingling once post-run).

Impression:
- Working impression: Right knee pain with mechanical symptoms (clicking during flexion/extension) consistent with overuse in the setting of increased running; transient swelling in the past; current exam shows full ROM with no reported locking or instability. ACL or meniscal injury not diagnosed via telemedicine; imaging and formal knee evaluation warranted if symptoms persist or worsen.

Plan:
- Continue ice therapy as currently used.
- Modify activity: ease up on running; avoid activity that provokes pain; if pain necessitates stopping, avoid continuing through pain.
- Medications: Continue ibuprofen as needed; a stronger anti-inflammatory prescribed by clinic (name not specified) to be taken with food and not concomitantly with ibuprofen; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Referrals/Imaging: Refer for physiotherapy assessment first for comprehensive knee evaluation; imaging (e.g., MRI) considered if indicated after PT assessment.
- Follow-up and red flags: If knee swelling, warmth/redness, high fever, or knee completely locks and cannot bend/stretch, seek urgent care and call back. If PT wait times are long, clinic visit possible.
- Pharmacy: Prescription for stronger anti-inflammatory to be sent to pharmacy.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Allergies not documented; full meds reconciliation not completed; vital signs and basic labs not provided; explicit imaging results not available (no prior imaging noted). 
- Internal conflicts: Conflict noted in transcript regarding knee ROM—patient initially suggested limited straightening but later affirmed full extension on direct questioning.
- Transcript quality: Generally coherent; some unit confusion (miles vs kilometers) and some redundancy; no major inaudible segments.
